recommendedGear.reason: Reliable quick-disconnect tow bar system for rapid unhooking in high-traffic urban staging lanes.

content.loopC: Perimeter sites offer the most straightforward backing angles and easiest swing-out clearance for long Class A rigs.
content.loopsAB: Interior rows are tightly spaced; drivers with long rigs should exercise caution when extending full-depth slide-outs.

name: Indian Rock RV Resort
address: 920 Province Line Rd, Cream Ridge, NJ 08514
summary: Pine Barrens border camping in Cream Ridge, NJ. Guidance on Province Line Road approach, soft sand interior shoulders, low pine branch clearance, and toad staging.

scorecard.toadFriendliness: High (spacious main office unhooking lot)
scorecard.treeClearance: Pine and oak canopy over interior sandy lanes; watch roof AC clearance

approach.title: Rural Highway & Entrance Clearance
approach.text: Province Line Road off Route 539 provides flat, clear access. The main gate entrance is wide, but watch for low pine branches hanging over the registration lane during summer growth.

recommendedGear.reason: Keeps big rigs on wide state and county connectors while avoiding narrow Pinelands backroads and low canopy shortcuts.

toadStrategy.text: Spacious unhooking area directly adjacent to the main office. Drop your toad here before proceeding down interior sandy lanes to avoid binding on sharp loop turns.

recommendedGear.reason: Includes quick-release levers that make unhooking effortless even on uneven sandy staging surfaces.

content.overview: Located near Six Flags Great Adventure, Indian Rock features heavily shaded pine forest sites. Soil is sandy with gravel overlay, requiring stable footing for jacks and levelers.

recommendedGear.reason: Sandy soil can shift under heavy rig jack pressure. Interlocking block stacks distribute weight evenly to prevent sinkage.

content.loopC: Pine Grove pull-through sites provide 50-amp full hookups with wide clearances suitable for large motorhomes and fifth wheels.
content.loopsAB: Back wooded loops feature soft sand shoulders along inner turning radiuses; keep trailer wheels on the firm gravel path.

name: Worthington State Forest
summary: Delaware Water Gap riverfront camping in Columbia, NJ. Ground-truth guidance on navigating narrow Old Mine Road, low-hanging overhead limbs, riverbank sloped gravel pads, and toad staging areas.

scorecard.maxRigLength: Up to 30 ft (strict physical length limits due to tight approach lanes)
scorecard.toadFriendliness: Low to Moderate (unhook at main office lot before entering Old Mine Rd loops)
scorecard.treeClearance: Low overhead canopy; frequent low-hanging riverbank branches along loop lanes
scorecard.bestBigRigLoops: Main Riverfront Loop (select back-in sites near entrance)
scorecard.bestSmallRigLoops: Upper Wooded Loops (best suited for camper vans, pop-ups, and small Class Cs)

approach.title: Old Mine Road & River Clearance Warning
approach.text: Access via Old Mine Road off I-80 is narrow, winding, and features rough pavement patches with soft shoulders. Overhead tree limbs hang low over the road in multiple sections, and single-lane pass points require extra vigilance for oncoming traffic when towing.

recommendedGear.reason: Provides custom routing and terrain awareness for narrow, unpaved, or low-canopy secondary state routes like Old Mine Road.

toadStrategy.text: Old Mine Road has minimal shoulder width to pull off if you encounter a tight pinch point. Disconnect your towed vehicle at the main park office lot near the entrance gate before driving into assigned loop lanes.

recommendedGear.reason: Provides clear rear coverage when staging, unhooking, and backing into shaded campsite loops.

content.overview: Tucked along the Delaware River in the shadow of Mount Tammany, Worthington State Forest offers a rustic water-gap setting. Sites are primitive (no electric hookups) with sloped gravel and dirt pads right along the riverbank.

recommendedGear.reason: Riverfront gravel pads slope downward toward the water. Solid rubber chocks combined with heavy-duty stackers prevent wheel creep on loose river gravel.

content.loopC: Riverfront back-in sites offer the easiest straight-line backing, but watch rear overhangs when positioning tires near the grassy bank edge.
content.loopsAB: Upper wooded loops are narrow with tight turning radiuses framed by mature trees, making them strictly suited for smaller travel trailers, camper vans, and truck campers.

name: The Great Divide Campground
summary: Sussex County family campground in Newton, NJ featuring open 50-amp G-Section pull-throughs (G20–G25) for 45-foot rigs, shaded woodland loops, a dedicated front-office toad staging lot, and direct County Route 519 access.

scorecard.maxRigLength: Up to 45 ft (G20–G25 open full-hookup pull-throughs)
scorecard.toadFriendliness: High — dedicated staging lot near front office before climbing interior hill grade
scorecard.treeClearance: Clear on County Route 519 & G-Section; moderate canopy on upper wooded back loops
scorecard.bestSmallRigLoops: Upper Wooded Back-In Loops (ideal for Class B/C motorhomes & sub-32 ft trailers)

approach.title: Highway & Interior Access Grade
approach.text: Direct approach off County Route 519 (from I-80 Exit 25 via US-206 North and CR-519, or from Newton via NJ-94/CR-519) is wide and smooth for all rig classes. Once inside the gate, climbing the main interior hill grade toward assigned upper loops requires steady momentum and prior toad staging.

recommendedGear.reason: Keeps big rigs routed cleanly onto US-206 and County Route 519 while avoiding narrow Sussex County backroads and low rural clearances.

toadStrategy.text: Pull into the dedicated staging lot near the main office immediately upon arrival and disconnect your towed vehicle on level ground before climbing the interior hill grade into assigned loops. Unhooking on an incline under tension risks binding your tow bar.

recommendedGear.reason: Provides clear rear visibility when staging near the office lot or backing into shaded upper woodland sites.

content.overview: Set across rolling Sussex County woodlands in Newton, NJ, The Great Divide Campground pairs wide, open big-rig pull-through sections with shaded forest perimeter sites, fishing lakes, pool, camp store, and family recreation minutes from Stokes State Forest and High Point.

recommendedGear.reason: Protects onboard air conditioners and sensitive electronics against peak summer voltage sags on 30/50-amp pedestals.

content.loopC: G-Section (specifically pull-through sites G20–G25) features full hookups, 50-amp service, wide turning geometry, and long level pads suited for Class A motorhomes and fifth wheels up to 45 feet.
content.loopsAB: Back wooded loops wind beneath mature hardwood canopy and require navigating a brief steep interior grade; best suited for travel trailers under 32 feet and Class B/C motorhomes.

name: Wading Pines Camping Resort
summary: Pine Barrens camping along the Wading River in Chatsworth, NJ. Ground-truth guidance on approach routes, overhead pitch pine clearance, 50-amp pull-through pads, and toad staging options.

scorecard.maxRigLength: Up to 45 ft (select oversized pull-throughs up to 60 ft)
scorecard.toadFriendliness: High (multiple unhooking options)
scorecard.treeClearance: Moderate overhead pine branches along interior sandy lanes

approach.title: Pine Barrens Route & Entrance Clearance
approach.text: Approaching via Route 563 to Godfrey Bridge Road is clear and flat. Watch for low-hanging pitch pine branches along the sandy entrance lane as you pull up to the gatehouse.

recommendedGear.reason: Keeps big rigs on wide state and county connectors while avoiding narrow Pinelands backroads and low canopy shortcuts.

toadStrategy.text: Unhooking up front can be tight during peak weekend check-ins. Either unhook directly on your pull-through pad or bypass the gate to the rear corner overflow lot.

recommendedGear.reason: Provides clear rear coverage when staging, unhooking, and backing into shaded campsite loops.

content.overview: Located deep in the New Jersey Pine Barrens along the Wading River.

recommendedGear.reason: Pine Barrens back-in sites feature soft sandy shoulders and subtle slopes. Having reliable chocks and interlocking blocks prevents shifting when parked on loose ground.

content.loopC: 50-amp pull-through sites offer straight pull-in convenience.
content.loopsAB: Inner wooded back-in loops feature soft sandy shoulders requiring leveling blocks.
